references.text: Jesus says the same words "Your faith has saved you" to the sinful woman who anointed his feet ([ref:Luk 7:50|Luke 7:50]). The expression "ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε" recurs as a fixed formulation used by Jesus when he acknowledges the power of faith.
Jesus says "Your faith has saved you" to the woman with bleeding who touched his cloak ([ref:Luk 8:48|Luke 8:48]). The same wording is used to show that faith is the decisive element in the healing.

Also to the Samaritan leper who returned to give thanks, Jesus says "Your faith has saved you" ([ref:Luk 17:19|Luke 17:19]). This pattern shows that faith and salvation/healing are inseparably linked in Jesus' ministry.

The parallel account in the Gospel of Mark about blind Bartimaeus at Jericho, where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "Your faith has saved you" and the man receives his sight ([ref:Mark 10:52|Mark 10:52]).
Jesus heals two blind men and says "It will be done for you according to your faith" ([ref:Matt 9:29|Matthew 9:29]). Here too, the healing of blindness is directly linked to individual faith.
Matthew's parallel account of two blind men at Jericho who cry out to Jesus and receive their sight ([ref:Matt 20:29-34|Matthew 20:29-34]). The same event described from a different perspective.
Mark's full account of the blind Bartimaeus who cries out "Son of David, have mercy on me" and is healed ([ref:Mark 10:46-51|Mark 10:46-51]). Parallel account to Luke 18:35-43.

Isaiah prophesies about the messianic age: "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened" ([ref:Jes 35:5|Isaiah 35:5]). Jesus' healing of the blind man is a fulfillment of this prophecy concerning the works of the Messiah.
The Lord calls his servant "to open the eyes of the blind" ([ref:Jes 42:7|Isaiah 42:7]). The healing of the blind man at Jericho shows that Jesus fulfills the prophecies about the Lord's servant.

In Jesus' programmatic speech in Nazareth, he quotes Isaiah and includes the mission to give "sight to the blind" ([ref:Luk 4:18|Luke 4:18]). The healing in Luke 18:42 is a concrete fulfillment of what Jesus declared as his mission.

Peter explains the healing of the lame man at the temple with the words "the faith that comes through him has given him this complete healing" ([ref:Apg 3:16|Acts 3:16]). Here too, faith is the central element in the healing, just as it was in Jesus' own ministry.
